key_insight: A single structure-preserving finite element framework can stably simulate geometric flows when bending energy depends jointly on orientation and curvature, while still guaranteeing discrete energy dissipation and exact area/volume conservation for constrained cases.
engineering_relevance: This provides a robust numerical tool for thin-structure and surface-shape optimization problems, including anisotropic shells and Helfrich-type models, where preserving physical invariants is critical.
method: Uses a fully discrete parametric FEM with continuous piecewise linear elements for curves and surfaces.
Couples geometry and curvature updates through a discrete energy inequality, aided by a surface energy matrix and mass-lumped projection of the curvature derivative.
Supports L2 flow, diffusion flows, and area/volume-constrained L2 flow under positivity and convexity assumptions on the density.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments with approximately second-order convergence in manifold distance and verification of the discrete energy, area, and volume preservation properties.
watch_item: The stability and energy guarantees rely on positivity, directional conditions, and convexity in curvature, so highly nonconvex or poorly conditioned anisotropic energies may require careful treatment.
paper_title: A unified structure-preserving framework for geometric flows with coupled orientation and curvature dependence
